0.title: A Structured Prompt
0.description: Copy-pasteable prompt for Claude.ai or ChatGPT that demonstrates structured prompting.
0.content:
Paste this into Claude.ai or ChatGPT — it's a structured prompt
that shows what the Research Agora skills do under the hood:

---
I'm writing a paper about [TOPIC] in [DOMAIN]. Diagnose my abstract:
- Does it have all 5 parts? (context, problem, approach, results, impact)
- Are claims specific or vague?
- What's the weakest sentence and how would you fix it?

[PASTE YOUR ABSTRACT]
---

When you're ready to move to the CLI, come back and run /onboard again.
0.followup: This is what structured prompting looks like. The Research Agora packages hundreds of these into reusable skills. When you're ready to move to the CLI, come back and we'll set up Claude Code.

1.title: Run Your First Skill
1.description: Execute a single skill matched to the user's stated task.
1.content:
Run your first skill — pick one based on your task:

  # Literature/references:
  claude "/paper-references"

  # Writing:
  claude "/paper-review"

  # Code:
  claude "/paper-verify-experiments"

That's it. One command, one result you can evaluate.
1.git_setup_hint:
If the user doesn't have git set up, offer to initialize it first:

cd /path/to/your/project
git init
git add -A && git commit -m "Initial snapshot before using AI agents"
1.followup: That's it. One command, one skill, one result you can evaluate. If it's useful, try another. If it's not, tell me what went wrong.

2.title: Set Up Verification
2.description: Walk through a verification pipeline that can be reused before every submission.
2.content:
Set up a verification pipeline:

  # 1. Snapshot your work
  git add -A && git commit -m "Before verification run"

  # 2. Run citation verification
  claude "/paper-references"

  # 3. Check paper-code consistency
  claude "/paper-verify-experiments"

  # 4. Get a simulated review
  claude "/paper-review"

Before your next submission, run steps 2-4.
2.followup: You now have a verification pipeline. Before your next submission, run steps 2-4. Treat it like running tests before a release.
2.zotero_note: The Zotero MCP can connect Claude Code directly to your library. Ask me to help configure it — takes about 5 minutes.

3.title: Build or Extend
3.description: For power users: contribute, orchestrate, or govern.
3.content:
You know the tools. Here's what scales:

- Package one of your existing workflows as a skill and submit a PR
- Explore research-agents: 22 agents for parallel claim verification,
  devil's advocate analysis, audience checking
- Use CLAUDE.md as a governance document — encode your lab's standards

paths.orchestration: Point to multi-agent patterns (research-agents plugin) and show how skills compose.
paths.contribution: Show the skill file format and suggest packaging an existing workflow as a skill.
paths.governance: Discuss CLAUDE.md as a governance document — encoding team standards, verification requirements, and review checklists.

3.followup: The Agora is built by researchers for researchers. If you've built a workflow that works, package it as a skill and submit a PR. That's how this thing grows.

steps: Try the structured prompts above for your immediate task
When you're ready for more: Install Claude Code (https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code)
Set up git as a safety net: Follow the 2-minute setup at https://rpatrik96.github.io/research-agora/git-backup.html — it gives you an undo button for agent edits
Come back: Run /onboard again once you have Claude Code — I'll set you up with skills
Save your CLAUDE.md to your project root
Set up git if you haven't already — it's your undo button for agent edits (https://rpatrik96.github.io/research-agora/git-backup.html)
Try 2-3 skills this week — see which ones stick
When something doesn't work: That's feedback. Adjust your CLAUDE.md or try a different skill
Level up: Once you're comfortable, explore the verification workflows (/paper-references, /paper-verify-experiments)
Save your CLAUDE.md and commit it to your repo
Snapshot before agent sessions: git add -A && git commit -m "Before: [task]" — see agent-specific git tips at https://rpatrik96.github.io/research-agora/git-backup.html#already-use-git
Integrate verification into your pre-submission checklist
Explore MCP tools: Zotero, arXiv, and GitHub MCPs extend what skills can do
Customize: Edit your CLAUDE.md as you learn what works — it's a living document
Share: If a colleague asks how you verified your citations, show them /onboard
Audit your current workflows — which ones are skill-shaped?
Package one workflow as a skill and submit it to the Agora
Explore research-agents: 22 specialized agents for devil's advocate analysis, evidence checking, audience alignment
Governance: Use CLAUDE.md to encode your lab's standards across projects
Benchmark: If you're working on evaluation, the Agora needs benchmark contributions — especially for citation hallucination detection
